Need current records and odds.I couldn't find anything that settles this yet. Kickoff is October 15, 10 days away, so the NFL scores page has no result and the question can't resolve Yes or No. Betting markets currently make Seattle a slight favorite at roughly 52–57%.

**What the resolution sources say (checked Oct 5, 2026)**
- **NFL.com:** I couldn't get the live scores page itself. NFL.com's Week 6 schedule page lists Seahawks at Broncos, Thursday, October 15th, 8:15 PM, PRIME, which matches the question. No score has been posted.
- **Metaculus FAQ (definition of "credible sources"):** I didn't retrieve this page. It only matters if the NFL page can't be used.

**The game**
- It's the 2025 champion's first trip to Denver. Denver will host the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. This will be the first time the Seahawks play in Denver since 2018.
- Seattle won Super Bowl LX in February 2026 under Mike Macdonald, after a 14–3 record in 2025. The team is led by quarterback Sam Darnold and the reigning Offensive Player of the Year, wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
- Both teams will wear colored throwback jerseys. The Broncos started wearing the orange throwbacks in 2024, and since then, they've worn them five times and gone 5-0.

**2026 form so far**
- **Seattle:** According to ESPN, they beat New England 13–10, won 31–7 at Arizona, and lost 33–31 at Washington. A Sportsnaut power ranking published today says they then beat the Chargers after leading by 21 midway through the third quarter. That gives them a 3-1 record, ranked 5th.
- **Denver:** According to ESPN, they lost 31–10 at Kansas City, then beat Jacksonville 20–13 and the Rams 30–26. The same ranking says San Francisco's defense kept the Broncos out of the red zone, which suggests Denver lost in Week 4 and is 2-2. I haven't confirmed that score.

**Games before Oct 15**
- Seattle hosts the 49ers on Oct 11 and then has a short week before travelling to Denver.
- Denver plays at the Chargers in Week 5 and then has its own short week.
- Injury reports will come out during the week of the game.

**Betting markets**
- **Sportsbooks:** DraftKings has Seahawks −1.5, moneyline −130 vs. Broncos +110, total 43.5. Caesars has SEA −125 / DEN −106 ([scoresandodds](https://www.scoresandodds.com/nfl/broncos-vs-seahawks)). VegasInsider, updated Oct 4, shows the line moving between Seattle −1.5 and −2.5. After removing the bookmaker's margin, that works out to roughly a 55–57% chance of a Seattle win.
- **Polymarket (seen Oct 5):** Seattle Seahawks at 52¢ (52% implied probability) and Denver Broncos at 49¢ (49%). The page didn't show trading volume or liquidity.

**History and base rates**
- **Head-to-head:** Total meetings: 58 - All-time series: Broncos: 35–23. The latest meeting was Sept 8, 2024, a 26–20 Seattle win, and Seattle has won the last two.
- **Home field:** Historically the home team wins about 55–57% of NFL games, and recently a little less. Thursday games give both teams short rest. That figure is general knowledge, not from today's searches.
- **Payton on Thursdays:** Denver is 1-0 on "Thursday Night Football" at home under Payton and 2-2 overall.
- **Ties:** NFL games end in a tie well under 1% of the time. A tie would resolve No.

**Note:** I found conflicting reports on Seattle's recent results. ESPN's page labels the Washington game as 9/27, while Sportsnaut has Seattle beating the Chargers. I treated the Chargers win as Week 4, but it's worth checking Seattle's exact results.

criterios: This question resolves YES if the Seattle Seahawks are recorded as the winning team of the NFL Week 6 regular-season game against the Denver Broncos, scheduled for Thursday, October 15, 2026 at Empower Field at Mile High (kickoff 8:15 PM ET / 6:15 PM MT). It resolves NO if the Denver Broncos are recorded as the winning team (including a Broncos win in overtime). The outcome is determined by the final score as reported on the NFL's official scores page (https://www.nfl.com/scores/) or by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
letra_pequena: If the game ends in a tie after overtime, the question resolves NO (the Seahawks did not win). If the game is postponed or rescheduled to a later date, resolution follows the actual played result whenever it occurs. If the game is cancelled outright and no result is recorded for the 2026 regular season, the question is annulled.
